parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Anjana Pillai (divorced wife) & Kum. Anagha (minor daughter)

facts_of_case: The couple was married and later divorced. The petitioners claimed maintenance for the wife and minor daughter under Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. The trial court partly allowed the application.

legal_principles.principle: A divorced wife is entitled to maintenance under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.
legal_principles.held: One main contention urged by the learned counsel for the appellants is that though the word 'Hindu wife' is used under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, it includes the divorced wife as well.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
cited_cases: Anjana Pillai vs P.Sasikumar on 7 January, 2016

legal_principles.principle: The quantum of maintenance granted in favour of the minor child is reasonable.
legal_principles.held: In regard to the minor child the amount of `5,000/- already awarded, is reasonable and there is no reason to interfere in that.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed and the quantum of maintenance granted in favour of the minor was increased.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
advising on grounds for divorce in Kerala
preparing a case for nullity of marriage
